center.summary: Return a copy of `a` with its elements centered in a string of length `width`.

count.summary: Returns an array with the number of non-overlapping occurrences of substring ``sub`` in the range [``start``, ``end``).

endswith.summary: Returns a boolean array which is `True` where the string element in ``a`` ends with ``suffix``, otherwise `False`.

expandtabs.summary: Return a copy of each string element where all tab characters are replaced by one or more spaces.

find.summary: For each element, return the lowest index in the string where substring ``sub`` is found, such that ``sub`` is contained in the range [``start``, ``end``).

greater.summary: Return the truth value of (x1 > x2) element-wise.

greater_equal.summary: Return the truth value of (x1 >= x2) element-wise.

index.summary: Like `find`, but raises :exc:`ValueError` when the substring is not found.

isalnum.summary: Returns true for each element if all characters in the string are alphanumeric and there is at least one character, false otherwise.

isalpha.summary: Returns true for each element if all characters in the data interpreted as a string are alphabetic and there is at least one character, false otherwise.

isdecimal.summary: For each element, return True if there are only decimal characters in the element.

isdigit.summary: Returns true for each element if all characters in the string are digits and there is at least one character, false otherwise.

islower.summary: Returns true for each element if all cased characters in the string are lowercase and there is at least one cased character, false otherwise.

isnumeric.summary: For each element, return True if there are only numeric characters in the element.

isspace.summary: Returns true for each element if there are only whitespace characters in the string and there is at least one character, false otherwise.

istitle.summary: Returns true for each element if the element is a titlecased string and there is at least one character, false otherwise.

isupper.summary: Return true for each element if all cased characters in the string are uppercase and there is at least one character, false otherwise.

less.summary: Return the truth value of (x1 < x2) element-wise.

less_equal.summary: Return the truth value of (x1 <= x2) element-wise.

ljust.summary: Return an array with the elements of `a` left-justified in a string of length `width`.

lower.summary: Return an array with the elements converted to lowercase.

lstrip.summary: For each element in `a`, return a copy with the leading characters removed.

mod.summary: Return (a % i), that is pre-Python 2.6 string formatting (interpolation), element-wise for a pair of array_likes of str or unicode.

multiply.summary: Return (a * i), that is string multiple concatenation, element-wise.

replace.summary: For each element in ``a``, return a copy of the string with occurrences of substring ``old`` replaced by ``new``.

rfind.summary: For each element, return the highest index in the string where substring ``sub`` is found, such that ``sub`` is contained in the range [``start``, ``end``).

rindex.summary: Like `rfind`, but raises :exc:`ValueError` when the substring `sub` is not found.

rjust.summary: Return an array with the elements of `a` right-justified in a string of length `width`.

rpartition.summary: Partition (split) each element around the right-most separator.

rstrip.summary: For each element in `a`, return a copy with the trailing characters removed.

slice.summary: Slice the strings in `a` by slices specified by `start`, `stop`, `step`. Like in the regular Python `slice` object, if only `start` is specified then it is interpreted as the `stop`.

startswith.summary: Returns a boolean array which is `True` where the string element in ``a`` starts with ``prefix``, otherwise `False`.

strip.summary: For each element in `a`, return a copy with the leading and trailing characters removed.

swapcase.summary: Return element-wise a copy of the string with uppercase characters converted to lowercase and vice versa.

title.summary: Return element-wise title cased version of string or unicode.

translate.summary: For each element in `a`, return a copy of the string where all characters occurring in the optional argument `deletechars` are removed, and the remaining characters have been mapped through the given translation table.

upper.summary: Return an array with the elements converted to uppercase.

assert_equal.summary: Raises an AssertionError if two objects are not equal.

assert_no_warnings.summary: Fail if the given callable produces any warnings.

assert_raises.summary: Fail unless an exception of class exception_class is thrown by callable when invoked with arguments args and keyword arguments kwargs. If a different type of exception is thrown, it will not be caught, and the test case will be deemed to have suffered an error, exactly as for an unexpected exception.

assert_raises_regex.summary: Fail unless an exception of class exception_class and with message that matches expected_regexp is thrown by callable when invoked with arguments args and keyword arguments kwargs.

assert_string_equal.summary: Test if two strings are equal.

assert_warns.summary: Fail unless the given callable throws the specified warning.

break_cycles.summary: Break reference cycles by calling gc.collect Objects can call other objects' methods (for instance, another object's __del__) inside their own __del__. On PyPy, the interpreter only runs between calls to gc.collect, so multiple calls are needed to completely release all cycles.

memusage.summary: Return memory usage of running python. [Not implemented]
